gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the DJI Power 1000 V2 has no solar or car input on the unit itself: DJI's manual lists only AC, SDC, SDC Lite and USB ports, so solar goes through a separately sold MPPT adapter module (labelled 400 W, panels in parallel only) and car charging through a separate SDC adapter.
standout_why: Compared against popsci.com (cited), willitrunpower.com, outagepowerguide.com and powersized.com, all opened 2026-11-27. None mentions SDC ports or a DJI adapter, and PopSci's under-$500 list does not include the DJI at all. willitrunpower already explains X-Boost / Power Lifting / SurgePad as voltage-lowering, resistive-only modes and that they do not count as motor-start surge, so that mechanism would score 0-1. ChatGPT's own second answer hints that 'some DJI charging accessories are proprietary' but gives no mechanism, limit or cost. It is not a 3 because it only decides the pick for shoppers who want solar or car charging.
decides: The DJI Power 1000 V2 stays the watts-per-dollar pick only for a shopper who recharges from a wall outlet and uses AC or USB. For solar or car charging, DJI needs an extra adapter, so the pick moves to a unit with the solar input built in. EcoFlow states 500 W for the DELTA 3 Classic and BLUETTI states up to 350 W for the Elite 100 mini; our record gives the Elite 100 V2 1,000 W at 12-60 V. That is the segment where one of ours (ALLPOWERS P1800 or a BLUETTI) can honestly win, but I could not re-read the P1800's solar input today. The BLUETTI page also confirms ChatGPT's 700 W limit on the Elite 100 mini: it states a 700 W total and shows no Power Lifting mode.

findings.label: Ports on the unit (DJI user manual v1.0)
findings.value: AC output ports, AC input port, SDC port, SDC Lite port, USB-A ports, USB-C ports; no XT60, car socket or direct PV input listed
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 User Manual v1.0 (EN)
findings.note: DJI's own PDF, read as text through the r.jina.ai reader because a direct fetch returned raw binary. I worked from an extraction summary, not the page images, so check the port list against the PDF before publishing.

findings.label: Solar charging path
findings.value: Through the DJI Power Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT), labelled 400 W in the manual's diagram; "Up to three solar panels can be connected to the adapter module and used in parallel (cannot be used in series)."
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 User Manual v1.0 (EN)
findings.note: The manual also lists a 1.8kW Solar/Car Super Fast Charger for the SDC port only. It gives no voltage limit, saying only "Make sure the connected solar panels are within the input specifications of the adapters."

findings.label: Car charging path
findings.value: Accessories only: Car Power Outlet to SDC Power Adapter, 1kW Super Fast Car Charger (SDC port only), or 1.8kW Solar/Car Super Fast Charger (SDC port only); "Make sure that the car engine is started before recharging."
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 User Manual v1.0 (EN)
findings.note: Same reading method as above. The only SDC cable figures in the manual are a default output of 13.6 V and a maximum of 10 A.

findings.label: UPS behaviour in DJI's words
findings.value: "The power station only supports the basic UPS feature and does not support 0ms switching." The manual gives no switch time in ms and says output power "may be lowered in UPS mode".
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 User Manual v1.0 (EN)
findings.note: The manual also says the AC output shuts down automatically after more than 30 minutes with no AC device drawing power, which matters for a load that cycles off for long stretches.

findings.label: MPPT adapter input limits (DJI Power Series FAQ)
findings.value: "When recharging DJI Power 1000 with solar panels, the DJI Power Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT) is required"; panel open-circuit voltage under 30 V; 200 W per XT60 input; 400 W per module
findings.note: This FAQ covers the original Power 1000 and the Power 500 and does not name the V2. The 400 W module figure matches the V2 manual's diagram; the 30 V and 200 W limits are DJI's figures for the same adapter, not a V2-specific statement. The FAQ also allows up to two modules on the original Power 1000.

findings.label: Built-in solar input, AC output and temperature limits (EcoFlow US spec page)
findings.value: Solar input 500 W max; AC output 1,800 W total at 120 V; X-Boost 2,600 W; UPS switch 10 ms; charge 0 to 45 °C (32 to 113 °F); discharge -10 to 45 °C (14 to 113 °F); 12.1 kg; 1,024 Wh LFP
findings.note: 12.1 kg × 2.2046 = 26.7 lb. The page gives no surge figure, no per-outlet amps, no solar voltage range and no footnote on X-Boost.

findings.label: Output limit and solar input (BLUETTI US store page)
findings.value: "Total output not to exceed 700W"; no Power Lifting mode mentioned on the page; up to 350 W solar; 10 ms UPS; 23.6 lb; $379.00 (was $429.00)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station, BLUETTI US
findings.note: The page shows "2–5 Business Days Delivery（Except for pre-sale products）". Its Tech Specs section came back empty in the fetch, so charge temperature was not read.

findings.label: What the rival pages already say about voltage-lowering modes
findings.value: willitrunpower: "EcoFlow X-Boost, BLUETTI Power Lifting and Anker SurgePad lower the output voltage so heaters and kettles keep working" and "Boost modes don't count" as motor-start surge
findings.source_title: Best power station under $500 (2026): picks by what you need to run | Willrun
findings.note: This is why the boost-mode mechanism is not the gap. The page's picks are priced as of Nov 19 and it does not list the DJI Power 1000 V2 or the DELTA 3 Classic.
